reasons: Rule fit is defensible: a USD 2,000,000/yr take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights means Customer pays a fixed shortfall sum for Services never received, which falls within the rule's detection scope (minimum fees / amounts payable by Customer that are untied to value delivered), and the payer is Customer as required.

Redline reaches the playbook preferred position (no LD, penalty, shortfall or minimum/early-termination charge payable by Customer) and is directionally correct — it removes the Customer-side commitment rather than merely softening it.

The 0.832 changed-character ratio is acceptable here: the rule requires excising the take-or-pay obligation, and the replacement sentence is a clean substitute rather than unrelated drafting; the added language stays within the rule's subject matter.

Comment is accurate on the cited clause, uses the required prefix and tone, explains the change, and offers the fallback (early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees) plus a commercial alternative (tiered pricing).

Minor, non-disqualifying points for the negotiator: (i) the rationale's 'walk-away' framing is overstated — a take-or-pay shortfall does not exceed remaining contract value; (ii) the drafted text bars any early-termination charge while the comment offers one as fallback, so expect to concede that carve-out; (iii) the cross-references to § 7.1 and § 12.3 were not in the supplied paragraphs and should be spot-checked before sending.
